1180: I started mountain biking at 15. Shortly after that I got into a downhill team and, with almost no experience, started racing straight away. Then I added four-cross, BMX racing and, in the last few years, enduro. I've raced in the Czech Cup and the World Cup. After almost 20 years on the bike, I love passing my experience on, whether to kids, men or women – and I love giving women the courage to see that you can have fun on a bike and that you can ride down anything. Even so, I keep trying to improve on the bike as much as time and my kids allow. RESULTS 2007 – national downhill champion 2008 – national downhill champion 2008 – national runner-up in four-cross 2008 – 6th place at the four-cross World Cup in Andorra Member of the Czech national downhill team
1181: Luky is another one of those who can't write a few lines about himself for his profile. A stubborn, pumped-up pocket-sized man capable of big jumps – and big crashes. He's considered our club's biggest die-hard in terms of work done, hours ridden and jumps crashed. Like Petr Jeřicha, Luky grew up on the bike alongside Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and worked his way up from village Trial rider to newcomer in the Elite category on 20″ trial bikes. He started at a later age, but he's clear proof that with regular training alongside better riders you can reach a decent level quickly and painlessly. He's into a whole range of other sports, including the opposite sex. After a short break and a one-year drop to the Expert category, he fulfilled his dream and won the Czech amateur championship title. RESULTSCzech champion, EXPERT categoryCzech runner-up, EXPERT categoryWinner of the 2015 OPEN FREE series4th place at the indoor cup in Germanyand many wins at Czech Cup races and open races ‍
1182: “Šimon” is one of the legends of the trial sport – a three-time world champion of the BIU (Biketrial) federation in the era before the world's riders left and the sport practically died out – and one of the most successful Trial representatives under the Czech Cycling Federation (UCI), winning the title of UCI world runner-up. Martin truly reached the very top of the Trial sport by competing at the world championships of both disciplines. Racing is no longer a priority for him, but even so he took second place in the 2011 Czech Trial Cup under the Czech Cycling Federation and won a number of Trial contests. Besides racing, he has collected and keeps collecting records on bikes – his biggest, still unbeaten record is riding up the Petřín lookout tower by hopping up the stairs, setting a time of 6:18 min on 30 March 1993. Today Martin focuses on exhibition performances and organising sports, cultural and social events as part of the TRIALSHOW.cz team. He can handle everything from hosting to management and logistics. He's a leading figure and a motivation for many riders, from beginners to the best Czech professional riders. RESULTS11x Czech champion6x Czech indoor championUCI world runner-up3x BIU world champion (back when that title was worth fighting for)and many more results that our screen resolution wouldn't be enough for … ‍
1183: ... whom nobody on the team calls anything but Čihi, is one of the most successful Czech Trial riders of the professional UCI federation, taught to ride by riders such as Martin Šimůnek, Josef Dressler and Roman Chvojka. He comes from the birthplace of the Czech trial sport, Říčany near Prague. He lives in Tehov, where he has some of the best conditions for his own training and that of his club colleagues.
